chapters.title: Measures to Mitigate Risks from Anonymous Instruments

articles.title: Subject matter
articles.requirement: Establishes rules on prevention of the use of the financial system for money laundering or terrorist financing

articles.title: Definitions
articles.requirement: Defines key terms: beneficial owner, PEP, business relationship, occasional transaction, shell institution, correspondent relationship, virtual IBAN, crypto-asset, etc.

articles.title: Obliged entities
articles.requirement: Defines which entities are in scope: credit institutions, financial institutions, auditors, notaries, lawyers, tax advisors, estate agents, high-value goods dealers, CASPs, football clubs, etc.

articles.title: Exemptions for certain providers of gambling services
articles.requirement: Member States may exempt certain gambling service providers from AMLR obligations based on proven low risk; must notify Commission; subject to conditions

articles.title: Exemptions for certain professional football clubs
articles.requirement: Member States may exempt professional football clubs not meeting high-value transaction thresholds; subject to risk assessment and Commission notification

articles.title: Exemptions for certain financial activities
articles.requirement: Member States may exempt persons conducting financial activity on occasional/limited basis where ML/TF risk is low; strict quantitative thresholds apply

articles.title: Prior notification of exemptions
articles.requirement: Member States must notify Commission and AMLA before granting exemptions under Art.4-6; AMLA may issue opinion within 2 months

articles.title: Notification of cross-border operations and application of national law
articles.requirement: Obliged entities operating cross-border must notify home and host supervisors; host Member State law applies to branches/agents operating in its territory

articles.title: Scope of internal policies, procedures and controls
articles.requirement: Obliged entities must establish and maintain proportionate internal AML/CFT policies, procedures and controls; approved by senior management; regularly reviewed

articles.title: Business-wide risk assessment
articles.requirement: Identify and assess ML/TF risks at entity level considering customers, countries, products, services, transactions and delivery channels; document and keep current

articles.title: Compliance functions
articles.requirement: Appoint compliance officer at management level with sufficient authority and resources; independent compliance function; direct reporting to management body

articles.title: Awareness of requirements
articles.requirement: Ensure all relevant employees are aware of AML/CFT requirements including data protection; regular training programme proportionate to role and risk

articles.title: Integrity of employees
articles.requirement: Screen employees in AML-relevant roles; fit and proper requirements; criminal record checks where permitted by national law

articles.title: Reporting of breaches and protection of reporting persons
articles.requirement: Establish confidential internal channel for reporting AML/CFT breaches; protect reporting persons from retaliation; anonymous reporting option

articles.title: Situation of specific employees
articles.requirement: Address specific risks posed by employees in sensitive positions; enhanced screening and monitoring where appropriate

articles.title: Group-wide requirements
articles.requirement: Group-wide AML/CFT policies, procedures and controls; information sharing within group; group-level risk assessment covering all subsidiaries and branches

articles.title: Branches and subsidiaries in third countries
articles.requirement: Apply EU-equivalent AML/CFT measures in third-country branches/subsidiaries; where local law prevents compliance, apply additional measures to manage risk; notify supervisors

articles.title: Outsourcing
articles.requirement: May outsource AML/CFT tasks; liability remains with obliged entity; must monitor and audit outsourced providers; specific conditions for third-country outsourcing

articles.title: Application of customer due diligence measures
articles.requirement: Apply CDD when establishing business relationship, carrying out occasional transactions >=EUR 10,000, suspecting ML/TF, or doubting previously obtained identification data

articles.title: Customer due diligence measures
articles.requirement: CDD measures comprise: identifying and verifying customer identity, identifying beneficial owner, assessing and obtaining information on purpose and nature of business relationship, conducting ongoing monitoring

articles.title: Inability to comply with customer due diligence requirements
articles.requirement: Where CDD cannot be completed: do not establish relationship or carry out transaction; terminate existing relationship; consider filing STR with FIU

articles.title: Identification and verification of customer and beneficial owner identity
articles.requirement: Collect identifying information (name, DOB, nationality, address, ID document); verify through reliable independent sources; identify beneficial owners (25% or more ownership interest, or control by other means)

articles.title: Timing of verification
articles.requirement: Verification must be completed before or during establishment of business relationship; deferred verification only in limited low-risk cases with specific safeguards

articles.title: Reporting discrepancies with beneficial ownership registers
articles.requirement: Report discrepancies between BO information obtained through CDD and information held in central beneficial ownership registers to the entity maintaining the register

articles.title: Identification of purpose and intended nature of business relationship
articles.requirement: Obtain information on the purpose and intended nature of the business relationship; level of information proportionate to risk profile of customer

articles.title: Ongoing monitoring of business relationship and transactions
articles.requirement: Conduct ongoing monitoring including scrutiny of transactions throughout the relationship to ensure consistency with knowledge of customer, business and risk profile; keep CDD information up to date

articles.title: Temporary measures for customers subject to UN financial sanctions
articles.requirement: Apply temporary measures where customer becomes subject to UN financial sanctions; immediate screening; restrict account activity pending further assessment

articles.title: Regulatory technical standards on customer due diligence information
articles.requirement: AMLA to develop RTS specifying minimum CDD information to be collected for different categories of obliged entities, customers and risk levels

articles.title: Identification of third countries with significant strategic deficiencies
articles.requirement: Commission identifies third countries with significant strategic deficiencies in AML/CFT regimes (FATF black list equivalent); triggers countermeasures under Art.35

articles.title: Identification of third countries with compliance weaknesses
articles.requirement: Commission identifies third countries with compliance weaknesses (FATF grey list equivalent); triggers enhanced due diligence measures

articles.title: Identification of third countries posing specific threats to the Union's financial system
articles.requirement: Commission may identify third countries posing specific ML/TF threats to the Union's financial system based on AMLA analysis; triggers specific countermeasures

articles.title: Guidelines on ML/TF risks, trends and methods
articles.requirement: AMLA issues guidelines on ML/TF risks, trends and methods to assist obliged entities in identifying suspicious activity; updated periodically

articles.title: Simplified due diligence measures
articles.requirement: SDD permitted where lower risk is identified through risk assessment; not a blanket exemption; must still identify customer and BO; reduced frequency/intensity of monitoring

articles.title: Scope of application of enhanced due diligence measures
articles.requirement: EDD required for: high-risk third countries, PEPs, complex/unusual transactions, and other situations presenting higher ML/TF risk; additional measures beyond standard CDD

articles.title: Countermeasures to mitigate ML/TF threats from outside the Union
articles.requirement: Specific countermeasures for high-risk third countries identified under Art.29: enhanced reporting, limiting business relationships, requiring senior management approval

articles.title: Enhanced due diligence for cross-border correspondent relationships
articles.requirement: Specific EDD for correspondent banking: assess respondent's AML controls, obtain senior management approval, understand responsibilities, ensure respondent has verified identity of customers with direct access

articles.title: Enhanced due diligence for crypto-asset service providers
articles.requirement: Specific EDD for CASPs in cross-border correspondent relationships; assess counterpart's AML controls; Travel Rule compliance; wallet address risk screening

articles.title: Specific measures for individual third-country respondent institutions
articles.requirement: Obliged entities may apply specific measures to individual respondent institutions in third countries based on their own risk assessment, beyond country-level measures

articles.title: Prohibition of correspondent relationships with shell institutions
articles.requirement: Prohibition on entering into or maintaining correspondent relationships with shell banks or institutions that allow shell banks to use their accounts

articles.title: Measures to mitigate risks from self-hosted addresses
articles.requirement: CASPs must apply specific measures for crypto-asset transfers involving self-hosted (unhosted) wallet addresses; verify ownership; apply EDD above certain thresholds

articles.title: Specific provisions for residence by investment scheme applicants
articles.requirement: EDD for applicants under residence/citizenship by investment schemes (golden visas/passports); enhanced source of wealth verification; senior management approval

articles.title: Specific provisions regarding politically exposed persons
articles.requirement: Determine whether customer or BO is PEP; apply EDD: senior management approval, source of wealth/funds, enhanced ongoing monitoring; applies to domestic and foreign PEPs equally

articles.title: List of prominent public functions
articles.requirement: Each Member State publishes and maintains list of prominent public functions qualifying as PEP; Commission consolidates EU-wide list; updated annually

articles.title: PEPs as beneficiaries of insurance policies
articles.requirement: Life insurance/investment: determine if beneficiary or BO of beneficiary is PEP; notify senior management before payout; apply enhanced scrutiny to relationship

articles.title: Measures for persons ceasing to be PEPs
articles.requirement: Apply risk-based measures for minimum 12 months after person ceases to hold PEP function; consider continuing influence, seniority, and role

articles.title: Family members and close associates of PEPs
articles.requirement: Extend PEP EDD measures to immediate family members (spouse, children, parents) and known close associates; apply risk-based approach

articles.title: Specifications for life and investment-related insurance sector
articles.requirement: Specific CDD provisions for life insurance and investment-related insurance; identify beneficiary and BO at time of payout; risk-based approach to verification

articles.title: General provisions on reliance
articles.requirement: May rely on third-party obliged entities for CDD; ultimate responsibility remains with relying entity; immediate access to CDD information on request

articles.title: Process of reliance on another obliged entity
articles.requirement: Specific process requirements for third-party reliance: written agreement, immediate data transfer, ensure third party is supervised and compliant; restrictions for high-risk third countries

articles.title: Guidelines on reliance
articles.requirement: AMLA to issue guidelines on conditions and processes for reliance on third parties; clarify scope and limitations; consider digital identity solutions

articles.title: Identification of beneficial owners for legal entities
articles.requirement: Legal entities must identify their beneficial owners; BO is any natural person who ultimately owns or controls the entity through direct/indirect ownership or other means

articles.title: Beneficial ownership through ownership interest
articles.requirement: BO through ownership interest: direct or indirect ownership of 25% OR MORE of shares, voting rights or other ownership interest (Art. 52(1) — inclusive at exactly 25%); indirect ownership calculated by multiplying down the chain and aggregating parallel chains

articles.title: Beneficial ownership through control
articles.requirement: BO through control: person exercising control through voting rights, right to appoint/remove board, shareholder agreements, or other means including de facto control

articles.title: Coexistence of ownership interest and control in the ownership structure
articles.requirement: Where both ownership interest and control exist in the ownership structure, all natural persons qualifying as BO through either criterion must be identified

articles.title: Ownership structures involving legal arrangements or similar legal entities
articles.requirement: BO identification must look through legal arrangements (trusts, foundations) and similar entities in the ownership chain; identify natural persons with ultimate control

articles.title: Notifications
articles.requirement: Beneficial owners must notify the legal entity of their BO status; legal entities must request and obtain BO information from their shareholders/members

articles.title: Identification of beneficial owners for legal entities similar to express trust
articles.requirement: For foundations, Anstalt, and similar entities: identify persons holding equivalent positions to settlor, trustee, protector, beneficiary, and any other person exercising ultimate control

articles.title: Identification of beneficial owners for express trusts and similar legal arrangements
articles.requirement: For express trusts: identify settlor, trustee(s), protector, beneficiaries (or class of beneficiaries), and any other person exercising ultimate effective control

articles.title: Identification of a class of beneficiaries
articles.requirement: Where beneficiaries of trusts/legal arrangements are designated by characteristics or class, identify the class with sufficient precision to establish identity when entitlement crystallises

articles.title: Identification of objects of a power and default takers in discretionary trusts
articles.requirement: For discretionary trusts: identify objects of a power of appointment and default takers; distinguish from fixed-interest beneficiaries

articles.title: Identification of beneficial owners of collective investment undertakings
articles.requirement: Specific rules for identifying BO of collective investment undertakings (funds); consider management company, fund manager, and material investors

articles.title: Beneficial ownership information
articles.requirement: Specify minimum BO information to be held: name, date of birth, nationality, country of residence, nature and extent of interest/control, date of becoming BO

articles.title: Obligations of legal entities
articles.requirement: Legal entities must obtain, hold, and keep up-to-date adequate, accurate and current BO information; submit to central register; update within defined timeframes

articles.title: Trustee obligations
articles.requirement: Trustees of express trusts and similar arrangements must obtain, hold and register BO information; disclose trustee status to obliged entities when entering business relationship

articles.title: Exceptions to obligations of legal entities and legal arrangements
articles.requirement: Limited exceptions to BO obligations: listed companies subject to equivalent disclosure requirements; certain regulated entities; conditions and safeguards apply

articles.title: Nominee obligations
articles.requirement: Nominees (acting on behalf of another person) must disclose nominee status and identity of nominator to the legal entity and to obliged entities

articles.title: Foreign legal entities and foreign legal arrangements
articles.requirement: Foreign entities/arrangements entering business relationship or acquiring real estate in EU must provide BO information equivalent to that required of EU entities

articles.title: Penalties
articles.requirement: Member States must lay down effective, proportionate and dissuasive penalties for breaches of BO transparency obligations by legal entities and arrangements

articles.title: Reporting of suspicions
articles.requirement: Obliged entities must promptly report suspicions of ML/TF to the FIU; report based on knowledge, suspicion, or reasonable grounds to suspect; no de minimis threshold

articles.title: Specific provisions for certain obliged entity categories
articles.requirement: Specific reporting provisions for lawyers, notaries, auditors and tax advisors: legal professional privilege considerations; may report through self-regulatory body in certain cases

articles.title: Refraining from carrying out transactions
articles.requirement: Obliged entities must refrain from carrying out suspicious transactions until they have reported to FIU; FIU may instruct to proceed or suspend; limited exceptions to avoid tipping off

articles.title: Disclosure to FIU
articles.requirement: Obliged entities must cooperate fully with FIU and respond promptly to FIU requests for information; provide all necessary documents and information

articles.title: Prohibition of disclosure
articles.requirement: Prohibition on disclosing (tipping off) that an STR has been filed or that ML/TF analysis is ongoing; exceptions for disclosure between group entities and between professionals involved in same transaction

articles.title: Threshold-based reports of transactions in high-value goods
articles.requirement: Persons trading in high-value goods must report to the FIU all sales of specified goods acquired for NON-COMMERCIAL purposes: motor vehicles at a price of at least EUR 250,000, and watercraft or aircraft at a price of at least EUR 7,500,000. Credit and financial institutions servicing the purchase or transfer of ownership of those goods must report such transactions too. Reporting within the deadlines set by the FIU.

articles.title: Exchange of information in partnerships
articles.requirement: Obliged entities may share information on ML/TF risks and suspicious activities within AML/CFT partnerships; subject to data protection safeguards; does not replace STR obligation

articles.title: Processing of personal data
articles.requirement: Processing of personal data for AML/CFT purposes is a matter of public interest under GDPR; must comply with data minimisation; no use for commercial purposes beyond AML/CFT

articles.title: Record retention
articles.requirement: Retain CDD records and transaction records for 5 years from end of business relationship or date of occasional transaction; maximum 10 years if justified; accessible to competent authorities

articles.title: Provision of records to competent authorities
articles.requirement: Records must be available and provided promptly to competent authorities and FIUs upon request; applies to both CDD records and transaction records

articles.title: Anonymous accounts and bearer shares
articles.requirement: Prohibition on maintaining anonymous accounts, anonymous passbooks, anonymous safe-deposit boxes; existing anonymous bearer shares must be converted to registered form

articles.title: Limits to large cash payments
articles.requirement: EU-wide limit of EUR 10,000 on cash payments accepted or made by persons trading in goods or providing services, whether in one operation or several that appear linked. Member States may set lower limits (notified to the Commission within 3 months); existing lower national limits continue to apply. Does not apply to payments between natural persons acting non-professionally, or to payments/deposits at credit institutions, e-money issuers and payment service providers.

articles.title: Cooperation between FIUs and European Public Prosecutor's Office
articles.requirement: FIUs cooperate with EPPO on financial crimes affecting the Union's financial interests; spontaneous and upon-request information exchange

articles.title: Requests for information to EPPO
articles.requirement: FIUs may request information from EPPO relevant to ML/TF analysis; EPPO responds through established cooperation channels

articles.title: Cooperation between FIUs and OLAF
articles.requirement: FIUs cooperate with OLAF on fraud, corruption, and other illegal activities affecting the Union's financial interests; information exchange protocols

articles.title: Requests for information to OLAF
articles.requirement: FIUs may request information from OLAF relevant to ML/TF investigations; reciprocal cooperation arrangements

articles.title: Exercise of delegation
articles.requirement: Conditions for Commission delegated acts under this Regulation; 4-year delegation period; Parliament and Council may revoke; scrutiny period

articles.title: Committee procedure
articles.requirement: Commission assisted by Committee on Prevention of Money Laundering and Terrorist Financing; examination procedure for implementing acts

articles.title: Review
articles.requirement: Commission to review and report on application of this Regulation by 10 July 2032; consider effectiveness, scope extension, new risks; consult AMLA

articles.title: Reports
articles.requirement: AMLA and Commission publish periodic reports on ML/TF trends, typologies, and effectiveness of national frameworks

articles.title: Relation to Directive (EU) 2015/849
articles.requirement: References in other instruments to AMLD4/AMLD5 to be read as references to this Regulation where applicable; correlation table in Annex VI

articles.title: Entry into force and application
articles.requirement: Enters into force 20 days after publication in OJ; applies from 10 July 2027; Art.5 (football clubs) applies from 10 July 2029
